candidates.title: Product change: A gold ring around your profile picture for 24 hours
candidates.what_is_different_here: Status is part of what Janitor Plus sells: the paywall promises a 'Golden checkmark next to your username' (s14.e12, gold badge s14.e25). The profile (s05) shows the avatar, username, follower counts and public profile link to other users in this creator community (characters, personas, scripts). A matching gold ring around the avatar extends that status for subscribers. It costs nothing to serve, and the profile is a safe screen. The ring is new and not sold, so it never undercuts the plan.
candidates.adds: A daily card on the profile lets subscribers play a short game to show a gold ring around their profile picture for 24 hours.
candidates.trigger_event: A Janitor Plus subscriber opens their own profile and has no ring active, at most once a day.
candidates.placement: A small card under the follower counts on the user's own profile.
candidates.offer_copy: Play a short game to add a gold ring around your profile picture, matching your golden checkmark, for 24 hours.
candidates.frequency_cap: 1 per day per subscriber, resets at midnight local time. Only offered while no ring is active.
candidates.decline_path: The card closes until tomorrow. The profile and golden checkmark stay exactly as they were.
candidates.ad_fail_path: If no game is available, the card does not show. If the game can't be confirmed, a short note says the ring wasn't added, and the subscriber can try again today.
candidates.subscriber_treatment: Only Janitor Plus subscribers see this offer, and the ring sits beside the golden checkmark they already have. Free users see no change.
candidates.advertiser_category: Casual mobile games and anime streaming

candidates.after_reward: When the 24 hours end, the ring fades and the card returns the next day, giving subscribers a reason to come back and keep their profile looking its best.
candidates.rationale: Subscribers already pay partly for a visible gold badge, so a matching ring that others can see is a reward they value. It costs the app nothing to serve. It brings ad income from users who otherwise see no ads, and it never touches what free users get or what the plan sells.

economics.assumption_line: Costs nothing extra to serve. The check can't tell whether it gives a place ahead of other users, which apps sell as a boost: no reward kind types visibility. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes no marginal serving cost; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).

candidates.title: Existing opportunity: Double the memory for your next 10 messages
candidates.what_is_different_here: Janitor Plus sells memory as a number: the paywall line '5× context for better memory' (s14.e09) and the headline 'More memory for long chats' (s14.e01). Users here run long stories. Chats with Miro show 12 chats with up to 17 messages each (s20), and replies averaged about 3,200 characters, so a long story quickly outgrows even 5× memory. A subscriber can only buy more of the same plan, and no higher tier was seen. A short boost from 5× to 10× for a few messages is the one thing this payer cannot get today. It sits in the side menu (s06) slot where free users see the upgrade banner (s06.e50), which is a safe screen away from chat content. The play pays only for the extra memory on messages the subscriber would send anyway.

reward.duration: next 10 messages in one chat, used by midnight local time

candidates.decline_path: The card closes and stays hidden until tomorrow. The plan's 5× memory works exactly as before.
candidates.ad_fail_path: If no game is available, the card does not show. If the game can't be confirmed, a short note says no boost was added, and the subscriber can try again today.
candidates.subscriber_treatment: Only Janitor Plus subscribers see this offer. It adds to the plan and never replaces it. Free users keep seeing the upgrade banner as today.
candidates.advertiser_category: Story-driven mobile games and streaming entertainment

flow_steps.caption: A subscriber opens the side menu as usual.

candidates.after_reward: After 10 messages the chat goes back to the plan's 5× memory, with a note that the boost can be played for again tomorrow, which brings the subscriber back daily.
candidates.rationale: Subscribers pay mainly for memory in long stories, and the paywall headline leads with it. A one-day doubling is the only way to get more. The play pays only for the extra memory on messages the subscriber was already sending, so it pays for itself in high-earning regions or with cheap serving. It also gives paying users a daily reason to open the app.

economics.assumption_line: Costs ~$0.0210 per reward to serve; pays for itself above $21.00 eCPM at 2k context ($36.00 at 8k). It may give away something the app could sell (more of the paid benefit l3 "5× context for better memory" to users who pay for it); that lost sale isn't counted. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes 10 replies of 800 tokens out, at $0.25 / $2.00 per million tokens in / out (central prices); the verdict uses the 8k figure; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).
